title: perf-bench-latency-throughput-maya-lopez-2026-03-22
content:
Quick perf scratchpad - Maya (working notes)
Date: 2026-03-22
Context / goal:
- Quick head-to-head latency+throughput runs for Llama2-13B-ish workload. Trying to verify impact of KV-cache + batching + low-precision integer kernels on end-to-end request latency and overall token throughput. These are developer-facing numbers (no SLA guarantees).

Environment:
- Model: custom-13b-rlhf (fp16 baseline, int8opt for quantized)
- Hardware: 1xA100-40GB (shared infra), isolated test pool
- Serving runtime: local branch maya/kv-batch-opt (based on PR #456)
- Inference server flags: --kv-cache=on/off, --batch-size=1/8, --quantize=int8/none, seq-len=512
- Client: curl/bench script that simulates 16 concurrent clients, prompt length ~40 tokens, gen length target 256 tokens
- Warmup: 200 requests (to populate GPU kernels & cache)

Command snapshots:
- baseline: ./bench --clients=16 --batch=1 --kv=off --quant=none --seq=512
- opt: ./bench --clients=16 --batch=8 --kv=on --quant=int8opt --seq=512

Raw summarized results (after warmup, avg of 3 runs each):

Config            | p50 lat (ms) | p95 lat (ms) | throughput (tokens/s) | notes
------------------|--------------:|-------------:|----------------------:|-------------------------
baseline (no KV)  |          210  |         480  |                   320 | batch=1, fp16 kernels
opt (KV + batch=8) |           85  |         160  |                   980 | int8 kernels, prefix cache helps

Observations / quick thoughts:
- KV cache clearly reduces tail latency and increases throughput; p95 drops ~3x.
- Batch=8 improved throughput significantly but added little to median latency due to continuous-batching path in runtime.
- Int8 quantization gave ~2-3x speed boost on throughput w/ minimal quality check (manual inspection of ~20 samples looks OK). Need eval run on eval-suite-1 to confirm quality.
- I saw a handful of 2-3 anomalous p95 spikes in run #2 for opt config (timestamps attached in raw logs). Might be logging jitter / GC on control plane or a noisy neighbor on shared GPU. Need to repeat on isolated dedicated node.

Quick diagnostics (notes to self):
- Check system logs around spikes: /var/log/redwood/serving/*.log (entries at 2026-03-22T14:12:03Z, 14:37:11Z)
- Confirm padding/batching semantics: are short requests being padded to 512 for kernel selection? If so, try dynamic-kernel selection by seq length (patch in PR-456).
- Validate int8 quantization with eval-suite: run eval-suite-1 (BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics + embed-sim) and compare to fp16 baseline.

Microbench notes (detailed):
- Token generation breakdown (opt config, avg): decode kernel ~30% time, attention KV memcopy ~12%, wandb logging overhead ~4% (we should disable logging in hot path for perf runs)
- Network overhead: internal RPC is ~8ms median per request in our setup; consider batching more client-side or colocating client with server for next run.

Next steps / TODO:
- [ ] Re-run opt config on dedicated-dev-2 (no noisy neighbors) and confirm tail stability (run 5x, collect p99).
- [ ] Run full eval-suite-1 against int8opt model; add results to CONFLUENCE-ENGINF-1122.
- [ ] File a follow-up small perf PR to reduce control-plane logging in hot path (Sam to review).
- [ ] Try intermediate batch sizes (4, 16) to find knee for latency-sensitive workloads.

Loose ideas / hypotheses to test later:
- Adaptive batching policy: prefer small batch for <50ms latency SLO, else batch aggressively for throughput.
- Cache-aware routing: route warm prefixes to nodes with large hot-KV caches.

References / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Confluence notes: CONFLUENCE-ENGINF-1122 (perf playbook)
- Jira: JIRA-ENGINF-789 (kv-cache followup)

Notes to collaborators:
- Sam: can you take a quick look at the log noise (14:12/14:37) and see if SRE had a scaling event?
- Ethan: please run eval-suite-1 for int8opt and drop results in the confluence page above.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into a formal lab report if numbers hold on dedicated hardware.

-- Maya
